title: A language-model approach to species distribution reveals alternative stable states
summary: In the journal abstract, a language-model-inspired generative model trained on about 27,000 reef-fish surveys produced alternative coral-associated and macroalgal-associated community configurations under identical environmental conditions. It also inferred core, bridging and satellite species positions and improved occurrence and biomass predictions over XGBoost and MLP baselines. The configurations are model-derived and consistent with previously described ecological regimes; independent field confirmation is not established by the abstract.
ai_technology: Language-model-inspired generative model for ecological communities
organization: Université de Montpellier; CNRS; Ifremer; IRD; Inria; University of Tasmania

evidence.tested: Fitted on about 27,000 reef fish surveys; predictive skill compared with XGBoost and MLP baselines; multistability interpreted against described ecological regimes.
evidence.unknown: Review limited to the indexed abstract and publication metadata; full-paper methods and additional limitations were not assessed.
evidence.ai_role: Generative language-model-style model that predicts each species and its biomass conditional on previously assembled species, used to generate community configurations.
